name: Comment Reply Bubble
what_you_see: TikTok/IG comment bubble overlaid on frame (e.g., 'Those seem so extra') with creator reacting beside it.
why_it_works: Social conflict + native UI; viewers want to see the response.
use_it: Use TikTok 'reply with video' sticker to a real objection comment.
also_called: reply to comment, comment sticker, skeptic comment

name: Kinetic Typography
what_you_see: Words pop/scale in one at a time, synced to speech or beat, dominant on screen.
why_it_works: Rhythmic reading keeps eyes locked.
use_it: CapCut auto-captions with bounce animation and keyword color.

name: Split Screen / Duet
what_you_see: Frame split into two (left/right or top/bottom) playing different clips simultaneously.
why_it_works: Two stimuli at once; comparison or reaction dynamic.
use_it: Top: problem footage; bottom: product fixing it.
also_called: side by side, duet layout, stacked screens

name: A vs B Comparison Graphics
kallaway_definition: Use graphics to showcase A vs B of something
what_you_see: Screen divided with labels (e.g., 'Theirs' vs 'Ours', 'Before' vs 'After') and graphics/checkmarks on each side.
why_it_works: Comparisons trigger instant judgement; brain wants to pick a winner.
use_it: Left: competitor product with red X; right: yours with green check; labels at top.
also_called: A vs B Graphics, this vs that, versus graphic, split comparison

name: Price Slash / Sale Tag
what_you_see: Old price with animated strike-through and new price or '% OFF' badge.
why_it_works: Loss aversion and deal-seeking.
use_it: Animate red slash over $89, show $39.

name: Circle / Highlight Annotation
what_you_see: Hand-drawn red circle or highlight box around a detail, often with zoom.
why_it_works: Mimics YouTube thumbnail cues: 'something is here'.
use_it: Circle the stain before/after or the tiny label.
also_called: red circle, highlight box, zoom circle

name: Image Overlay Motion
kallaway_definition: Use an image (with or without motion) and text to begin the video
what_you_see: Begins on an image (with or without Ken Burns motion) plus text headline instead of live video.
why_it_works: Clean readable composition delivers the idea instantly.
use_it: Use a striking product photo with slow zoom and bold claim text.
also_called: photo + text opener, still image opener

name: Text/Arrow Pointer
kallaway_definition: Use text and an arrow to direct attention at some visual while explaining what it is
what_you_see: Arrow(s) and short label point at a detail in the image (a feature, a flaw).
why_it_works: Directs gaze precisely; implies something noteworthy hidden in plain sight.
use_it: Freeze on product close-up, red arrow + 'this saved me $300'.
also_called: arrow callout, pointer graphic, annotation arrow

name: Bold Headline Text Box
what_you_see: Large high-contrast text block (white box/black text or outlined) dominating the top third from frame 1.
why_it_works: Readable in silent autoplay; frames the value instantly.
use_it: Overlay a 6-8 word claim in TikTok-native font over any UGC opener.
also_called: text-on-screen hook, caption block, big text

name: Breaking News Lower Third
what_you_see: TV-news style lower third/ticker ('BREAKING:') over footage.
why_it_works: Authority and urgency cues borrowed from news.
use_it: Creator as anchor with banner 'BREAKING: this sold out 3x'.

name: Handwritten Sign / Paper Note
what_you_see: Creator holds a handwritten sign/paper with a message, possibly flipping it.
why_it_works: Low-fi human authenticity; readable without sound.
use_it: Hold sign 'I tried every acne cream' then flip to product.
also_called: paper sign, cardboard sign, note reveal

name: Meme Caption Frame
what_you_see: Video letterboxed inside a white top bar with meme-style black caption.
why_it_works: Native meme grammar reads as entertainment, not ad.
use_it: Put funny relatable caption above product fail clip.

name: Social Post Screenshot
what_you_see: A tweet/Reddit post/Amazon review card fills the screen or sits over the creator (green-screen style).
why_it_works: Borrowed credibility and relatable complaint.
use_it: Green-screen creator in front of a Reddit thread about the problem.
also_called: tweet overlay, reddit screenshot, review screenshot

name: Tier List Board
what_you_see: Opens on an S/A/B/C/F tier-list board being filled with products or options.
why_it_works: Rankings trigger opinion and the urge to see where their pick lands.
use_it: Screen-record or overlay a tier board; drag competitors into low tiers and your product into S tier.

name: Interactive Title
kallaway_definition: Use the title text to create motion by having it come on the screen in an interesting way
what_you_see: Title text appears in an interesting way - creator pushes, catches, or is revealed from behind it.
why_it_works: Text becomes a physical object in the scene, breaking the 2D plane.
use_it: Creator 'pulls down' the headline like a blind to reveal product.

name: Screen Recording w/ Motion
kallaway_definition: Start with a screen recording using motion to aim the viewer's attention
what_you_see: Starts with a phone/desktop screen recording that zooms/pans to guide the eye to a specific element.
why_it_works: Familiar UI + motion guidance; implies proof or tutorial.
use_it: Screen-record the Shopify order notification or review page and zoom on the key number.
also_called: screen rec zoom, app screen hook

name: Small Image Drop Overlay
kallaway_definition: Use a small image to drop on a larger image and integrate the small subject into the large
what_you_see: A small image (logo, product, face) drops/bounces onto a larger background image and integrates into it.
why_it_works: Unexpected element entering composition; scale contrast.
use_it: Drop a PNG of the product onto a lifestyle photo with bounce animation.

name: Text Slide In
kallaway_definition: Title text slides into video
what_you_see: Headline text slides in from an edge over the opening footage within the first second.
why_it_works: Motion on text draws eye to message before audio.
use_it: Keyframe the benefit headline sliding in from left over product B-roll.

name: Big Stat Callout
what_you_see: Giant number (e.g., '93%' or '$10,000') occupies the frame.
why_it_works: Specific numbers imply evidence and scale.
use_it: Show '2,000,000 sold' counter animating up.

name: Fake Text / iMessage Thread
what_you_see: iMessage/WhatsApp/DM bubbles popping in over footage asking about the product.
why_it_works: Voyeurism into private conversation + social proof.
use_it: Animate a friend asking 'where did you get that??' bubble by bubble.
also_called: text message hook, DM screenshot, chat bubbles

name: Motion-Tracked Text
what_you_see: Label/text pinned to a moving object/person via tracking.
why_it_works: Text feels part of the physical scene.
use_it: Track 'this is $12' to the bottle as creator waves it.
also_called: text stuck to object, tracked label

name: Numbered Listicle Title
what_you_see: Big number + list headline ('3 reasons your skin...') with number '1' marker.
why_it_works: Promises finite, skimmable payoff.
use_it: Title '5 things I wish I knew before buying X', '#1' tag on first item.

name: Redacted / Censored Bar
what_you_see: Key word/brand hidden behind a black bar, blur, or emoji.
why_it_works: Withheld info creates curiosity gap.
use_it: Blur product name in the headline until reveal.

name: Watch Till The End Text
what_you_see: Explicit 'wait for it' / 'watch till the end' overlay over teaser footage.
why_it_works: Explicit open loop commitment.
use_it: Overlay over satisfying build-up footage.
also_called: wait for it, end payoff caption

name: Whiteboard Explainer
what_you_see: Hand drawing a diagram on a whiteboard/paper in real time.
why_it_works: Watching a drawing form = process curiosity.
use_it: Sketch 'problem -> product -> result' quickly.

name: Countdown
kallaway_definition: Start the video by counting down from 3, 2, 1 before revealing something
what_you_see: On-screen numbers 3, 2, 1 before revealing something.
why_it_works: Countdowns create built-in anticipation and a promised payoff.
use_it: Big 3-2-1 over covered product, reveal on 'go'.

name: Journal Story Highlight
what_you_see: Handwritten journal page with brand name highlighted by marker.
why_it_works: Intimate diary voyeurism + highlight draws eye.
use_it: Highlight product name in handwritten entry.

name: Poll / Guess Sticker
what_you_see: Question with A/B options or a guess prompt overlaid on a mystery visual.
why_it_works: Invites participation; viewers commit to an answer.
use_it: Show extreme close-up of product texture with 'Guess what this is?'

name: Search Bar Typing
what_you_see: Search bar UI with a query being typed and autocompleted.
why_it_works: Familiar UI mirrors the viewer's own question.
use_it: Animate 'how to get rid of...' typing then show product.

name: Spec Callout Lines
what_you_see: Product hero shot with thin lines/dots pointing to labeled features that draw in.
why_it_works: Premium tech-product aesthetic; organized information.
use_it: Rotate product and animate 3-4 feature callouts.

name: Star Rating / Review Card
what_you_see: 5 gold stars and a quoted review line over product footage.
why_it_works: Instant social proof heuristic.
use_it: Stars animate in one by one over hero shot.

name: Beat Match Visual Switch
kallaway_definition: Edit the timing of the clips turning on matched to the beat of the song
what_you_see: Clips switch exactly on music beats in the first seconds.
why_it_works: Audio-visual synchrony is pleasurable and propulsive.
use_it: Cut 4 product shots to a trending sound's beats.
also_called: Beat Match Switch, beat sync cuts, cuts on the beat

name: Camera Wipe
what_you_see: Something (hand, object, person) passes across the lens, wiping the frame into a new scene.
why_it_works: Occlusion + reveal resets attention.
use_it: Swipe product across lens, reveal after-state.

name: Match Cut
kallaway_definition: Use a rapid series of visuals/text that line up
what_you_see: Rapid series of shots where shapes/positions/text line up across cuts.
why_it_works: Visual continuity with content change feels clever and hypnotic.
use_it: Product circle lid -> moon -> cup rim cuts aligned at center.

name: Rapid Flash Montage
what_you_see: 4-8 very short (0.1-0.3s) shots in the first 1.5 seconds.
why_it_works: Novelty density overwhelms scroll reflex.
use_it: Cut 6 product close-ups and reactions in 1.5s.
also_called: jump cut montage, 0.2s cuts, quick cuts

name: Viral Stitch Linked Reaction
kallaway_definition: Start with a viral clip and then react to it as a transition into your video
what_you_see: Opens on a recognizable viral clip, then cuts to creator reacting and linking it to the topic.
why_it_works: Borrowed attention from a proven clip + curiosity about the link.
use_it: Stitch a viral fail related to the problem, cut to founder: 'this is why we made X'.
also_called: stitch reaction, react to viral clip

name: Genre Bait-and-Switch
what_you_see: Opens like a different genre (horror, nature doc, cooking show) then reveals it's a product ad.
why_it_works: Prediction error when genre breaks.
use_it: Nature-documentary style shot of 'wild' product, then cut to UGC.
also_called: fake-out, looks like a movie trailer

name: In Media Res Start
what_you_see: Video begins mid-sentence/mid-argument/mid-chaos with no setup.
why_it_works: Missing context forces viewer to catch up.
use_it: Start on creator mid-rant with product in hand.

name: Multi-Creator Mashup
what_you_see: Rapid succession of different people each showing the product.
why_it_works: Social proof + face variety.
use_it: Cut 5 UGC creators saying one word each.

name: Stitch Interview Mic-In-Face
what_you_see: Handheld mic thrust toward a stranger on the street, question asked.
why_it_works: Spontaneity and real-person reactions.
use_it: Ask shoppers 'what are you looking for?' and hand product.
also_called: street interview opener, man on the street

name: Visual Switch
kallaway_definition: Use an action in the first shot to cleanly transition to the second shot
what_you_see: An action in shot 1 (cover lens, spin, clap) cleanly transitions into shot 2.
why_it_works: Continuity of motion masks the cut; payoff is the new scene.
use_it: Cover lens with product box, uncover in new setting.

name: Freeze Frame Record Scratch
what_you_see: Action freezes suddenly (often with record-scratch), with a label or narration intro.
why_it_works: Classic sitcom trope; motion stop is jarring.
use_it: Freeze on creator mid-spill: 'yep that's me. you're probably wondering...'

name: Photo Collage to Video
what_you_see: Starts as a static collage of photos that snaps into live video.
why_it_works: Format switch resets attention.
use_it: Collage of customer photos animating into UGC clip.

name: Remote Control Channel Switch
what_you_see: A remote clicks and the scene/product variant changes stop-motion style.
why_it_works: Interactive feel; each click is a mini-reveal.
use_it: Click through each colorway of the product.

name: Viral Stitch Unlinked Switch
kallaway_definition: Use a viral clip (high anticipation) and then cold switch to a clip of your brand/business
what_you_see: High-anticipation viral clip, then a cold hard cut to unrelated brand/business footage.
why_it_works: Anticipation from clip carries over; the jarring switch is itself the hook.
use_it: Open on a crazy stunt; cut before resolution to founder at desk.
also_called: cold switch, bait and switch clip

name: Fake Crash / Phone Drop
what_you_see: The camera appears to fall/crash; frame tumbles, cracks, or goes black.
why_it_works: Simulated accident = startle and concern.
use_it: Film phone dropping onto a bed, add crack overlay, cut to case ad.

name: Transformation Cover Cut
what_you_see: Hand/cloth covers the lens then reveals a transformed look (hair, skin, room).
why_it_works: Instant before/after payoff.
use_it: Cover lens with palm, reveal after using product.
also_called: hand over lens transformation, glow-up cut

name: Unexpected Interruption
what_you_see: A second person barges into frame/scene mid-speech.
why_it_works: Social disruption hooks curiosity about who and why.
use_it: Partner walks in: 'that tip you gave me worked'.
also_called: someone walks in, partner interrupts, husband's surprise

name: Viral Stitch Motion Match
kallaway_definition: Start with a viral clip and then match cut your own motion to match
what_you_see: Starts with a viral clip, then your footage matches its motion (e.g., same swing/throw).
why_it_works: Continuation illusion links borrowed attention to your brand.
use_it: Viral basketball throw clip -> your product caught in matching motion.

name: Fly on Wall
kallaway_definition: The subject of the video is looking off screen. Common in podcast interview style clips
what_you_see: Subject is looking off screen (not at lens) mid-conversation, like an interview or podcast clip, framed from a side angle.
why_it_works: Voyeur effect: feels like overhearing something real rather than being sold to.
use_it: Seat founder/customer at 45 degrees, interviewer off camera; open on a mid-answer punchy line about the product.
also_called: looking off camera, podcast side angle, observational

name: Many of Same Prop
kallaway_definition: Multiple items. Could be similar or different
what_you_see: Frame filled with many units of the same (or similar) item - a pile, grid, or stack.
why_it_works: Abundance/scarcity signal and pattern density demand a second look.
use_it: Arrange 30 units of the product on bed or counter, creator sits behind them.
also_called: stack of products, product pile, multiple items, wall of units

name: Move In Frame
kallaway_definition: Creator walks into or around the frame to give motion to the eye
what_you_see: Frame starts empty or on a background; the creator walks/leans/steps into shot from an edge within the first second, often ending close to lens.
why_it_works: Motion onset is the strongest pre-attentive attention trigger; an empty frame filling creates mini-anticipation.
use_it: Lock phone on tripod, start recording on empty kitchen/bathroom, walk in holding the product and stop at mid-shot.
also_called: walk into frame, walk-in, enter frame

name: Mid-Action Demo Start
what_you_see: Video begins with the product already working mid-task (vacuum sucking, blade cutting, serum applied).
why_it_works: Immediate proof; TikTok recommends showing the product in action right away.
use_it: Cut the first 2s of the demo clip away so frame 1 is peak action.
also_called: in media res demo, product in action, demo first

name: Pour / Splash
what_you_see: Liquid, powder or cream being poured/splashed in close-up, often onto the product or a surface.
why_it_works: Fluid motion is hypnotic and satisfying.
use_it: Pour coffee on a stain-proof shirt; splash water on waterproof gear.

name: Holding Prop
kallaway_definition: Subject starts by holding/looking at a prop, which becomes focus of POV shot
what_you_see: Creator starts holding or staring at an object close to camera; the object dominates the frame.
why_it_works: Object curiosity + gives the eye a concrete focus before words.
use_it: Open with the product held 20cm from the lens, creator glancing at it then camera.
also_called: prop in hand, product in hand opener, hold up product

name: Mirror
kallaway_definition: Creator talks to audience from reflection in mirror
what_you_see: Creator addresses the audience via a mirror reflection; the phone may be visible.
why_it_works: Familiar get-ready framing reads native; reflection composition is visually layered.
use_it: Film skincare/apparel pitch in bathroom mirror with product on sink.
also_called: mirror talk, reflection shot, mirror selfie

name: Squeeze / Squish
what_you_see: Close-up of fingers squeezing, pressing, peeling, or stretching a soft product.
why_it_works: Tactile ASMR mirror-neuron satisfaction.
use_it: Macro shot of thumb pressing into memory foam or peeling a pimple patch.

name: Sunglasses On
what_you_see: Creator puts on sunglasses (or takes them off) in the first second before speaking.
why_it_works: Confident gesture + motion onset; meme-familiar.
use_it: Creator slides on shades while holding product, 'deal-with-it' vibe.
also_called: put on sunglasses, deal with it

name: Camera Whip
kallaway_definition: Use fast camera whip motion to create initial stun
what_you_see: Frame 1 is a fast horizontal/vertical camera swing with heavy motion blur that snaps to the subject or product.
why_it_works: Blur-to-sharp resolution creates a mini 'arrival' moment; motion blur reads as energy.
use_it: Handheld: start pointed at wall, whip fast to product on counter and stop hard; add whoosh SFX.
also_called: whip pan, swish pan, camera whip pan

name: Yap Cold Open
kallaway_definition: Creator starts talking to audience and there is nothing happening in visual hook
what_you_see: Creator just starts talking to camera; nothing special happens visually. The hook rides entirely on the first spoken line and on-screen title text.
why_it_works: Baseline talking-head start: zero production, feels native. Works when the first sentence and title text are strong enough on their own.
use_it: Film yourself mid-thought holding the product, open on your strongest line, and put a punchy title text on screen from frame 1.
also_called: mid-sentence open, cold open talking head, already talking

name: Object Into Lens
what_you_see: Product (or hand) moves rapidly toward the lens until it fills/blacks out the frame.
why_it_works: Looming motion triggers a defensive startle reflex.
use_it: Creator thrusts the product at the phone until it blocks the lens, cut to next shot.
also_called: push to lens, throw at camera, product to camera, shove in lens

name: Problem Reenactment
what_you_see: Exaggerated acting out of the problem (hair frizz, back pain, spilling) before the product appears.
why_it_works: Instant self-identification with the pain.
use_it: Creator dramatically fails at the task the product fixes.

name: Rip-Open Unboxing
what_you_see: Hands tearing tape/box/bag open with product about to emerge.
why_it_works: Anticipation of reveal; TikTok names unboxing a proven opener.
use_it: Top-down shot of hands slicing the mailer and pulling the product out.

name: Rock-Paper-Scissors / Coin Flip
what_you_see: Two creators play RPS or flip a coin on camera with labels (save money vs buy product).
why_it_works: Game outcome suspense; viewers predict the winner.
use_it: Label each hand with text overlay; product always 'wins'.

name: Wake Up / Bed Start
what_you_see: Creator lying in bed/on floor, often shot from above, before sitting up.
why_it_works: Vulnerable, unusual horizontal framing.
use_it: Top-down bed shot, creator sits up and grabs product from nightstand.

name: Object Catch
kallaway_definition: Catch item thrown into frame
what_you_see: An object flies into frame from off-screen and the creator catches it, usually the product.
why_it_works: Unpredicted incoming motion triggers reflexive tracking.
use_it: Off-camera helper tosses product; creator catches at chest height and starts talking.
also_called: catch thrown item, throw and catch

name: Point To Visual
kallaway_definition: Start with creator on screen and then use finger to point to focus visual
what_you_see: Creator on screen in frame 1 immediately points (finger or both hands) up/sideways at a product, graphic or text block that sits beside/above them.
why_it_works: Gaze-and-gesture cueing: viewers reflexively follow a pointing finger to the target.
use_it: Green-screen or split the frame: creator bottom half points up at a product shot or claim text top half.
also_called: point at graphic, finger point hook

name: Setting Down Phone
kallaway_definition: Set down recording device as video starts
what_you_see: First frames are shaky as the recording device is placed on a surface, then settle on the creator already talking.
why_it_works: Feels raw/unscripted (native, not an ad) and implies urgency.
use_it: Hold phone, record while placing it against the bathroom mirror/car dash, then start the pitch.
also_called: phone set down, prop camera, sit-down start

name: Destruction / Stress Test
what_you_see: The product (or rival) is hit, dropped, crushed, cut, burned, or run over in the first frames.
why_it_works: Violence to objects + 'will it survive?' curiosity.
use_it: Drop phone case from head height onto concrete; stand on the bottle.
also_called: smash test, drop test, durability test, torture test

name: Face Lean-In to Lens
what_you_see: Creator's face lunges toward lens into extreme close-up, eyes filling frame.
why_it_works: Intimacy/looming face triggers social attention circuits.
use_it: Lean in to whisper the 'secret' benefit.

name: Hand Grab From Off-Screen
what_you_see: A hand enters the frame and grabs the product off a surface (or out of someone's hand).
why_it_works: Implied desire/competition for the item.
use_it: Static product shot, hand swoops in and snatches it.

name: Stop-Hand To Lens
what_you_see: Creator shoves an open palm or 'stop' sign to the lens in the first frame.
why_it_works: Literal command gesture + looming hand.
use_it: Palm at lens, pull back to reveal product in other hand.
also_called: palm to camera, stop scrolling gesture

name: Walking Backward Talk
what_you_see: Handheld selfie while walking (often backward) through a busy space, background moving.
why_it_works: Constant background motion keeps eyes engaged; feels vlog-native.
use_it: Founder walks through warehouse or street holding phone at arm's length.

name: Framebreaker
kallaway_definition: Remove background from initial visual and overlay it on a normal background so subject appears to break the frame
what_you_see: Subject is cut out and layered so part of it (hand, product, head) breaks over the border of a framed photo/box, appearing 3D.
why_it_works: Depth illusion violates the flat-screen expectation.
use_it: Rotoscope the hand holding product so it pokes out of a white-bordered card over a blurred background.
also_called: frame break, pop-out effect, out of bounds

name: Fridge POV
kallaway_definition: Put camera in fridge, cabinet, food aisle, etc, and then remove item/open door to reveal creator
what_you_see: Camera placed inside a fridge/cabinet/drawer/shelf; the door opens or item is removed to reveal the creator looking in.
why_it_works: Unusual vantage point + 'being seen by an object' novelty.
use_it: Put phone on fridge shelf behind the product; creator opens door and grabs product.
also_called: inside the fridge POV, cabinet POV, shelf POV

name: Jump Switch
kallaway_definition: Creator jumps and when they land the scene changes
what_you_see: Creator jumps; on landing, the location/outfit/product has changed.
why_it_works: Action-matched change feels seamless and surprising.
use_it: Jump in old clothes, cut at apex, land wearing product/in new room.
also_called: jump transition, jump cut outfit change, land in new scene

name: Post-It / Cover Reveal
what_you_see: Product (or answer) is hidden under a post-it, cloth or cardboard that is peeled/pulled away.
why_it_works: Curiosity gap: hidden object demands the reveal.
use_it: Stick a question post-it on product front; peel it in first second.
also_called: sticky note reveal, cover pull, cardboard reveal

name: Money Throw
what_you_see: Bills thrown into the air around creator.
why_it_works: Money is a primal attention magnet; chaos motion.
use_it: Toss prop cash while announcing a sale.

name: Unusual First Image/Scene
kallaway_definition: Use a full screen image of something that visually breaks conventional pattern
what_you_see: A full-screen image or scene that visually breaks convention (odd object, bizarre place).
why_it_works: Novelty detection.
use_it: Product in a bizarre spot (bathtub full of product).

name: 3D Talking Character
what_you_see: Frame 1 is a 3D/Pixar-style or claymation character (an organ, pill, body part, germ, animal or product) looking at camera and talking, often in a real-world set.
why_it_works: An unexpected cartoon character in a feed of real people breaks the pattern and personifies the problem.
use_it: Generate a character of the problem (e.g. a tired liver, a hair follicle) with an AI image/video tool and have it deliver line 1 straight to camera.
also_called: Talking Organ, Pixar-style mascot, AI character opener, Claymation character

name: Animal / Pet Hook
what_you_see: Pet in frame doing something cute or funny with product.
why_it_works: Universally attractive stimulus.
use_it: Dog 'reviewing' the pet product.

name: Baby / Kid Hook
what_you_see: Baby or child in frame reacting/using product.
why_it_works: Protective attention bias.
use_it: Toddler trying the product with parent reaction.

name: Before/After Result Shot
what_you_see: Opens directly on the result or side-by-side before/after.
why_it_works: Instant proof payoff.
use_it: Show result first, then how.

name: Celebrity / Famous Clip
what_you_see: Recognizable celebrity/meme face in the first frame.
why_it_works: Face recognition triggers attention.
use_it: Licensed or meme clip relevant to benefit (use carefully).

name: Gross / Problem Close-Up
what_you_see: Close-up of the problem: dirty filter, blackheads, stain, mold.
why_it_works: Disgust grabs attention; self-check.
use_it: Show the gunk in an old pillow.

name: High Motion Base B-Roll
kallaway_definition: The core base visuals have high motion embedded in them
what_you_see: The base footage itself contains high motion (sports, vehicles, crowds, splashes).
why_it_works: Motion-rich frames beat static talking heads.
use_it: Use product in motion: bike ride, workout, pouring.

name: Car Talking Head
what_you_see: Creator in driver's seat talking, parked.
why_it_works: Native, authentic UGC setting.
use_it: Film car review for car accessory.

name: Absurd Prop
what_you_see: Creator uses an absurd prop (banana as microphone, giant clock).
why_it_works: Humor + incongruity.
use_it: Oversized prop version of product.

name: Archival / Vintage Footage
what_you_see: Old film grain footage or historical photo.
why_it_works: Nostalgia + contrast.
use_it: Vintage ad clip then modern product.

name: CCTV / Security Cam Look
what_you_see: Grainy, high-angle, timestamped security footage.
why_it_works: Voyeuristic realism.
use_it: Doorbell-cam style: package delivered, dog steals.

name: Chaos / Mess Scene
what_you_see: Opens on a messy, chaotic room/situation.
why_it_works: Disorder draws scanning.
use_it: Messy closet before organizer.

name: Lo-Fi Native Selfie
what_you_see: Vertical front-camera selfie, casual lighting, no graphics.
why_it_works: Looks like a friend's post.
use_it: Creator's phone front cam in real home.

name: Microscope View
what_you_see: Microscope/magnified imagery of skin, fabric, bacteria.
why_it_works: Invisible world revealed.
use_it: USB microscope on skin before/after.

name: First-Person POV Hands
what_you_see: Camera at eye level showing the viewer's own hands using the product.
why_it_works: Self-projection.
use_it: Chest mount or head-height shot of hands opening the product.

name: Low-Angle Hero Product
what_you_see: Low-angle product shot with dramatic lighting.
why_it_works: Monumentality.
use_it: Shoot product from table level against backlight.

name: Macro ASMR Close-Up
what_you_see: Extreme macro of texture: cream swirl, fabric weave, bubbles.
why_it_works: Sensory detail rarely seen; ASMR satisfaction.
use_it: Macro lens on product texture.

name: Oddly Satisfying Process
what_you_see: Perfectly clean process: peeling film, cutting, pressure washing, perfect fit.
why_it_works: Completion satisfaction.
use_it: Peel protective film off product; pressure wash a stain.

name: Out-of-Place Element
what_you_see: Orderly scene with one element clearly not belonging.
why_it_works: Anomaly detection.
use_it: Neat vanity with a live lobster beside product.

name: Silent Reaction PIP
kallaway_definition: Creator watches a base clip silently and then reacts
what_you_see: Base clip plays while creator in a small corner box watches silently, then reacts.
why_it_works: Emotional contagion; curiosity about reaction.
use_it: Founder in corner watching a customer video, reacts.

name: Megaphone Announcement
what_you_see: Creator shouting through a megaphone.
why_it_works: Urgency and noise cue.
use_it: Announce sale through megaphone.

name: Unusual Location
what_you_see: Creator in odd place: shopping cart, washing machine, car trunk, freezer aisle.
why_it_works: Setting incongruity.
use_it: Pitch skincare sitting in a bathtub full of clothes.

name: Visual Mistake
kallaway_definition: Add something unexpected (that often looks like an error or glitch) to the frame
what_you_see: Something that looks like an error (misplaced object, weird crop, mis-framed shot).
why_it_works: Brain fixates on anomalies.
use_it: Leave a deliberate 'mistake' (camera upside down, product half-out).

name: Empty Shelves / Sold Out
what_you_see: Empty store shelves or 'sold out' signs.
why_it_works: Scarcity.
use_it: Film empty display in store.

name: Lab / Side-by-Side Experiment
what_you_see: Two containers/samples side by side with labels being tested.
why_it_works: Evidence framing.
use_it: Two cups: competitor vs yours.

name: Green Screen Composite
what_you_see: Creator cut out over an image/article/website/product page background.
why_it_works: Credibility of source + native TikTok look.
use_it: Creator over the product page or an article about the problem.

name: X-Ray / Cutaway 3D
what_you_see: 3D render showing inside body/product (how it works).
why_it_works: Seeing the invisible.
use_it: 3D animation of product fibers or gut bacteria.

name: Time-lapse / Hyperlapse
what_you_see: Hours compressed into seconds (plant growth, cleaning, melting).
why_it_works: Visible change at unnatural speed.
use_it: Time-lapse of the stain vanishing over 30 minutes.

name: Crazy Transitions
kallaway_definition: Using high motion editing transitions or templates in Capcut
what_you_see: High-motion editing transitions: spins, zoom blurs, glitch, shake, from templates.
why_it_works: Visual energy + novelty.
use_it: Apply a CapCut trending template to product shots.

name: Experimental (Interactive)
kallaway_definition: Use motion graphics on screen to suggest thumb movement, and then edit to match the motion
what_you_see: On-screen motion graphics that suggest the viewer's thumb (swipe/tap), then the edit responds.
why_it_works: Hijacks the scrolling gesture itself; feels interactive.
use_it: Animate a fake 'tap here' hand icon; video 'responds' by zooming to product.
also_called: fake swipe, thumb interaction, fake UI tap

name: AI Morph / Transformation
what_you_see: One object/person morphs smoothly into another (old product morphs into new).
why_it_works: Continuous impossible change.
use_it: Morph competitor bottle into your bottle.

name: The Zoom In
kallaway_definition: Zoom in on creator
what_you_see: Slow continuous zoom toward creator's face/product from frame 1.
why_it_works: Subtle intensification signals importance; cinematic tension.
use_it: Digital slow zoom 100->115% on founder saying the claim.

name: Blur-to-Focus
what_you_see: Opens blurred (text or subject) and slowly/sharply comes into focus.
why_it_works: Brain needs to resolve unclear information.
use_it: Blurred claim on paper racks into focus; or foreground product racks to face.
also_called: rack focus, blurred focus technique, depth of field pull

name: FOOH / CGI Product Stunt
what_you_see: CGI product doing the impossible in real environment (giant lipstick on a bus, bottle on a building).
why_it_works: Looks real yet impossible.
use_it: AI video generator composite of product over city skyline.
also_called: fake out of home, 3D product in city

name: Snap Zoom / Zoom Punch
what_you_see: Instant zoom (jump or 2-4 frame ramp) into face/product on a key word.
why_it_works: Sudden scale jump = emphasis and jolt.
use_it: Punch in 130% on 'ONE product'.

name: Stop Motion
what_you_see: Product moves in choppy frame-by-frame steps, assembling or walking itself.
why_it_works: Handcrafted novelty; objects 'alive'.
use_it: Shoot 20 photos moving product box, play at 12fps.

name: Fish Eye
kallaway_definition: Film using a fish eye lens to give a different look
what_you_see: Barrel-distorted ultra-wide image, faces/products bulge at center.
why_it_works: Distortion is novel and playful.
use_it: Clip-on fisheye lens, product pushed to the camera.

name: Look Up At Camera // Top Down
kallaway_definition: Film using a camera up in the corner of a room to give a different look
what_you_see: Camera placed high in a room corner or overhead; subject looks up at it.
why_it_works: Unusual angle reads like security cam/surveillance.
use_it: Stick phone high on the kitchen wall, creator looks up.
also_called: top-down CCTV angle, high corner cam, overhead

name: Sudden Danger 1P POV
kallaway_definition: Use clip of a dangerous thing about to happen to viewer and fast switch/stitch
what_you_see: First-person view of something dangerous heading toward the viewer (ball, car, dog), cut at the moment.
why_it_works: Self-threat triggers visceral startle.
use_it: POV of product flying at face, cut to creator.

name: Dolly Zoom
what_you_see: Subject stays same size while background stretches/compresses.
why_it_works: Uncanny spatial warping signals realization.
use_it: Walk phone backward while zooming in on product.

name: Giant / Miniature Scale Illusion
what_you_see: Product appears huge next to people/buildings or creator appears tiny.
why_it_works: Scale violation grabs attention instantly.
use_it: Forced perspective: product close to lens, person far away 'holding' it.
also_called: forced perspective, giant product, tiny person

name: Reverse Footage
what_you_see: Motion plays backward - product flies up into hand, liquid returns to glass.
why_it_works: Physics violation.
use_it: Drop product, reverse clip so it jumps back into hand.
also_called: reverse drop, rewind physics, reverse motion

name: Slow Motion Hero
what_you_see: Ultra slow-motion of action (hair flip, splash, crumble).
why_it_works: Reveals invisible detail; luxurious feel.
use_it: 240fps shot of serum drop hitting skin.

name: Zoom Out Reveal
what_you_see: Starts extreme close on a detail, pulls out to reveal full surprising context.
why_it_works: Recontextualization payoff.
use_it: Close on texture; pull back to show it's the product in use.

name: Color Switch
kallaway_definition: Use any visual, start with 0 saturation, change to full color on tap/beat
what_you_see: Opens in grayscale (0 saturation) and snaps to full color on a tap/beat.
why_it_works: Color onset is a strong pre-attentive trigger.
use_it: Grey 'before' scene turns vivid when product used.
also_called: black and white to color, desaturation pop

name: Speed Ramp Effect
kallaway_definition: Add a speed ramp transition in the edit from shot 1 to shot 2
what_you_see: Footage speeds up then slows (or vice versa) across the transition from shot 1 to shot 2.
why_it_works: Time distortion is dynamic and cinematic.
use_it: Ramp a pour to slow-mo at splash.

name: Freeze Frame
what_you_see: Motion stops dead on a frame with a highlight or text.
why_it_works: Motion-to-stillness contrast.
use_it: Freeze mid-splash with label.

name: Glitch / VHS / Datamosh
what_you_see: Pixel smearing, RGB split, scan lines or datamosh artifacts.
why_it_works: Looks like a malfunction; brain checks.
use_it: Glitch transition into the product reveal.
also_called: glitch effect, vhs filter, digital error

name: Jump Out of Phone
what_you_see: Creator appears to exit a phone/TV screen into the real world.
why_it_works: Impossible 2D-to-3D crossing.
use_it: Composite creator stepping out of phone with product.

name: Mask Reveal Transition
what_you_see: A new scene appears within a moving object's silhouette (door, arm, product).
why_it_works: Layered reveal.
use_it: Mask 'after' scene within the product as it passes.

name: Vanish / Magic Disappear
what_you_see: Object or person disappears with a snap/poof effect.
why_it_works: Object permanence violation.
use_it: Make the clutter vanish, leaving organizer.
